title: Decision: a did:key may be an alsoKnownAs inside a did:webvh log; mimid never accepts one as a credential
description:
Mark, 2026-11-22, decision 2 of the five the bridge and identity work raised (bead mimid-5ltz, which holds the three readings in full).

CONTEXT. meshIRCd's identities are mostly did:key; mimid's are did:webvh (draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential). A did:key proves possession of a key now and nothing about who held it over time, because there is no log to replay; the log is the whole point of did:webvh.

CHOSEN: a did:key may appear as an alsoKnownAs entry inside a did:webvh log. The log remains the only authority. The did:key is a second name the same person publishes, signed by the user's own update keys like everything else in the log, so a provider cannot put one there. mimid never accepts a did:key as an MLS credential in its own right.

WHY NOT THE OTHERS. Refusing outright would leave the two systems sharing only a display convention, and a person present in both unrecognisable as one person. Accepting did:key as a peer of did:webvh in a credential would change the scope of Mark's own draft, need a place in the credential codec, and need a rule for what a room's policy makes of an identity with no log and no witnesses — a weaker identity in the same slot as a stronger one.

IT ALREADY WORKS AT THE CREDENTIAL LAYER. mimi_mls::didwebvh::mimi_user_uri takes the one alsoKnownAs entry whose scheme is 'mimi:' and ignores every other entry (crates/mimi-mls/src/didwebvh.rs), so a did:key entry passes verification today, untouched and unread. No change to the credential, the codec or the verifier.

WHAT IS LEFT, filed separately: a reader beside mimi_user_uri for the did:key entries of a verified log, and somewhere to show them, so a meshIRCd identity and a mimid one are recognisably the same person. The reader must not assume one entry: unlike the mimi: URI, which is one or none, a person may publish several keys.
